nodes.label: signatory
nodes.rationale: A person whose name is printed on a report's signing line, not necessarily a system user. Kept as its own table rather than a flag on user, so someone like the PENR Officer who never logs in can still be a signatory and so a staff member leaving does not disturb the signatory history.

nodes.label: signatory history row
nodes.rationale: One row per version of a signatory's name and position title, with a date range saying when that version was in use. The date range belongs to the row, not the person, so overlapping ranges for one person are valid rather than an error.

nodes.label: reports reference a history row, not stored text
nodes.rationale: A typo and a real name change need opposite behaviour. Storing the name as text on each report freezes both alike, so a misspelling would be permanent across every record that used it and nobody would remember which records those were. With a foreign key to a history row, editing the row fixes a typo everywhere, while ending the row and creating a new one preserves old reports through a marriage or promotion. Consequence - the UI must offer 'Fix a spelling mistake' and 'This person's name changed' rather than a plain Edit button.

nodes.label: position title typed on the signatory row
nodes.rationale: Suggested from the person's record but never read live from it, because titles change with promotion or acting assignment and old reports must keep the title as it was printed.

nodes.label: signing line / slot
nodes.rationale: One printed line on a report such as 'Prepared by' or 'Approved by'. The actual list of lines is still unknown (Topic 5) and blocks writing the table that joins reports to signatories.

nodes.label: signatory roster
nodes.rationale: The list of who is currently expected to sign which line, used to suggest names when a report is made.

nodes.label: one person may hold several signatory rows at once
nodes.rationale: The same person can be an active signatory under more than one position title simultaneously - for example Chief of the Environmental Management Division and OIC-PENR Officer - and the report preparer picks the right one.

nodes.label: OIC needs no separate feature
nodes.rationale: The agency has no formal way of assigning an Officer-in-Charge - the next in rank signs informally - so a feature with start and end dates would mirror a process that does not exist. An OIC is just another signatory row with the acting title typed in and a date range, which the multiple-rows rule already supports.

nodes.label: signing happens both on paper and in the system
nodes.rationale: Unresolved consequence - some lines can never be approved in the system because the signer has no account, so a 'signed on' date is permanently empty for them. Without a marker the system cannot tell 'not signed yet' from 'will never be signed here', which matters for deciding whether a report is complete. Proposed but not agreed - mark each line as approved-in-system or printed-only.

nodes.label: signatory conflict checker
nodes.rationale: Five candidate conflicts, none agreed - duplicate row, ambiguous suggestion, signatory whose account is gone, same person on two lines of one report (probably allowed, since the brief permits self-approval), and gap in coverage (arguably the most useful, since it blocks completing a report).

nodes.label: Topic 10 - full separation of employee and user
nodes.rationale: Chosen over 'employees only for non-users' (which scatters the office's people across two tables) and 'let user be the employee table' (which makes the login code responsible for always excluding password-less rows, easy to get wrong later). Recording every employee closes the Topic 3 gap where a signatory without an account had nothing to link to, and an employee list has value on its own. Cost - a real migration moving the name fields out of user, small at fewer than twenty users with no production data.

nodes.label: no reports for periods before go-live
nodes.rationale: Only reports from go-live onward, so historical signatory assignments with past dates never need loading.
